A.label: Historical ORCS H01: Philosophy and Logic
A.claim: The source's H01 manifest identifies House 01 as Philosophy and Logic.

B.label: Aluminum OS H01: Science
B.claim: The source's v4.0 draft lists H1 as Science; an H01 identifier here is edition-specific.

synthesis.hypothesis: A+B=C: two source-indexed ontologies reuse H01 with incompatible House semantics, therefore federation must retain edition-qualified coordinates and refuse same-as mapping until separately reviewed.
counterevidence: Both House taxonomies may legitimately discuss overlapping subjects such as philosophy of science; a reviewed RELATED mapping is possible without an EQUIVALENT identity claim.
The Aluminum document is versioned as a draft; its source-authority description cannot automatically govern the Ariadne v0.7 ontology.
falsification_tests: Compare full pinned H01 source definitions and separately signed crosswalk acceptance before attempting semantic joining.
Run a negative joining test: H01 alone must not conflate Philosophy and Logic with Science across editions.
Verify current source rights and revocation at each eventual Work reader and output action.

house_review.risk: Ontology ambiguity can misclassify energy or physical-science claims.
Water and food topics may be assigned to an incompatible historical House.
Circular infrastructure records may inherit wrong ontology identities.
Health evidence may be misrouted across namespaces.
Publication, extraction and scientific review remain separate evidence states.
A fabricated coordinate equivalence may cross a security access boundary.
Financial conclusions cannot inherit authority from an ontology name.
Translation across cultural knowledge systems can erase context.
Epistemic disagreement must be preserved instead of auto-resolved.
Community sources require explicit permission and representation.
Rights revocation and consent take priority over archive continuity.
Space and aerospace source meaning is not established by H12 in legacy ORCS.
